origins.section: Four Racing Workers and a Wall Clock Give a Different Plan Each Run
The Medium Season Now Repeats, Byte for Byte

gates.says: all 3 of this quiz's answerable readings held and each was taken over the question as it stands

recorded.prompt:q-cause: Read the whole lesson page, then this question. Using only what the page states, which option does the page decide is correct? Quote or cite the deciding passage.
recorded.outcome:q-cause: a **wall-clock limit** stops the search at a different point each run, because the same work takes a different number of seconds on a busy machine; and **parallel workers race**, so which worker's plan is best at the moment of the stop depends on thread timing.
recorded.prompt:q-wall: Read the whole lesson page, then this question. Using only what the page states, which option does the page decide is correct? Quote or cite the deciding passage.
recorded.outcome:q-wall: The record keeps no timestamp and no wall time: those differ every run by nature, and a record that holds them can never compare equal.
recorded.prompt:q-price: Read the whole lesson page, then this question. Using only what the page states, which option does the page decide is correct? Quote or cite the deciding passage.
recorded.outcome:q-price: a fixed limit of 10 units of work buys a plan anyone can reproduce; more work buys a better one, and stays reproducible as long as the limit is part of the record.
